slides.title: Agentic AI Systems Engineering
slides.subtitle: Designing, building, securing and operating enterprise agents that plan, reason, use tools and remember — across five days and one system that grows with you.
slides.notes: Welcome. Introduce yourself in one minute, then go straight to the failure story on the next slide — do not spend ten minutes on logistics. Housekeeping goes in the chat or on a printed card. Confirm everyone ran `make doctor` and got 8/8; floaters help anyone who did not while you start.

slides.statement: An LLM answers. An agent acts.
slides.attribution: And anything that can act can act wrongly, at scale, spending money and touching personal data.
slides.notes: Say it, pause, let it land. The whole week is the engineering consequence of that one sentence: bounded loops, structural authorisation, observation. Do not explain it yet.

slides.title: Saudi enterprises are past the chatbot
slides.intro: The shift from answering to acting changes the risk profile entirely — and that is an engineering problem, not a prompting one.

bullets.text: Reschedule a delivery, open a case, reconcile an invoice, move money. The agent is now inside the business process, not beside it.
An agent can be wrong while running perfectly. There is no exception, no stack trace, no red dashboard — just a confidently wrong action.
PDPL applies to what the agent remembers. An automated money movement needs an audit trail a regulator accepts.
The reasoning pattern you default to is worth a 20x swing in cost per contact. That is invisible in a demo and fatal at 18,000 contacts a day.
Prompting people do not think about budgets and idempotency; platform people do not think about non-determinism. This course lives exactly at that seam.

aside.title: THE MAXIM
aside.body:
As much structure as possible, as much agency as necessary.

You will hear this on every day of the week. By Friday you will be able to say where, in your own code, the line sits — and defend it with a measurement.

slides.notes: Ask the room: who here has an agent in production? Who has one in a pilot that leadership already believes is production? The gap between those two answers is the course.

slides.title: One system, five days: Rafeeq at Tawseel

steps.sub: M8 · a test, not a poke

slides.caption: Rafeeq (رفيق) is an operations assistant for Tawseel (توصيل), a fictional Saudi last-mile logistics company. Every lab extends the same system — nothing is thrown away, and Friday's capstone is an assembly, not a scramble.
slides.notes: This slide is the map. Come back to it at the start of each morning and point at where the class is. Say explicitly: there is no weather agent in this course.

slides.title: What you will own by Friday afternoon

cards.title: A deployed service
cards.body: Rafeeq running in a simulated Tawseel environment behind /v1/resolve, containerised, with health and readiness endpoints, resolving bilingual tickets end to end.

cards.title: Evidence it works
cards.body: An evaluation harness over 120 labelled tickets and 60 TawseelBench scenarios, with measured task success, cost per contact, p95 latency and zero cross-customer leakage.

cards.title: A security report
cards.body: A red-team suite running in CI over 78 attack payloads in Arabic and English, triaged findings, structural mitigations, and zero open high-severity.

cards.title: Trade-off literacy
cards.body: DECISIONS.md: five engineering decisions you can defend — pattern per workflow, where authorisation lives, cache key design, single versus supervisor, escalation policy.

slides.notes: Stress the second card. The point of the course is that the system testifies to its own quality — grading is evidence-first, demo second.

slides.title: How the week runs

items.text: Every lab extends Rafeeq. Nothing is throwaway.
Every claim needs a measurement. "It worked in the demo" never counts.
Cheap model by default; the frontier model is reserved for the capstone demo.
Pairs rotate daily — a strong prompter with a strong engineer.
Code, state keys and commits in English. Rafeeq itself is bilingual.
Lab completion — checkpoint commits and expected outputs
PA-1 diagnosis and PA-2 security report
Flagship Expert badge needs ≥70 overall, capstone ≥70, zero open high-severity, and a green leakage test

slides.notes: Say the cost rule out loud and point at the shared spend board. Cost literacy is a graded outcome, not a courtesy.

slides.title: Before we start: the five-minute check

127 assertions pass with no API key and no network
exported, with your per-participant spend cap visible on the board
optional today — needed from Lab 3 onward for the MCP and Qdrant stack
